prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a low-speed head-on collision. Plain text. Call the parties only 'Plaintiff' and 'Defendant'. No names, placeholders, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1449; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant generally denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition and in any amendment or supplement thereto, and demands strict proof thereof as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure. Pursuant to Rule 92, Defendant further asserts the following affirmative defenses.

First, Plaintiff's alleged injuries were not proximately caused by any negligence of Defendant. The collision was of low speed and the forces involved were insufficient to cause the injuries claimed, and any condition Plaintiff now complains of predates the occurrence or arises from unrelated causes.

Second, Plaintiff failed to mitigate damages by unreasonably delaying or declining recommended medical treatment, and any recovery must be reduced accordingly.

Third, Plaintiff's own negligence caused or contributed to the occurrence. Under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, any recovery must be reduced by the percentage of responsibility attributed to Plaintiff, and if that percentage exceeds fifty percent, Plaintiff may not recover.
